findings.title: Ollama listens beyond loopback
findings.evidence: DEMO: recognized Ollama process on TCP 0.0.0.0:11434.
findings.explanation: The listening address is not restricted to the local loopback interface.
findings.limitation: Reachability from another device, firewall rules, internet exposure and authentication were not tested.
findings.action: If remote access is unnecessary, ask the service owner to restrict the listening address to loopback. Otherwise review firewall restrictions and authentication. Do not change a shared service without its owner.
findings.verification: Run this check again and confirm the intended binding. Ask IT to validate required remote access separately.

findings.title: Review local command connection in Claude Desktop (1)
findings.evidence: Claude Desktop: declared MCP entry 1 in %APPDATA%/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json → mcpServers; local command; activation state not verified; URL scheme: not configured; URL user-info present: False; auth-related setting present: False; enabled_tools list count: None; disabled_tools list count: None. These are configuration facts, not effective permissions or proof of authentication. Raw identities and secret values are excluded.
findings.explanation: An MCP connection is configured. These connections can extend an assistant’s capabilities.
findings.limitation: Configuration does not prove the connection is running, has broad permissions, or is unsafe. Command arguments, environment values, tokens and conversation contents are not included in this report.
findings.action: Open %APPDATA%/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json → mcpServers and locate entry 1 in the declared server table (file order, not sorted display order). Confirm its owner, purpose, allowed tools, data destinations and approval settings. Review command arguments locally; do not paste credentials into the report.
findings.verification: Record the owner and permission review. A rescan can confirm configuration presence, not that permissions are appropriate.

findings.title: Document permitted work use of AI
findings.evidence: You reported work use of AI and no agreed rules for that use.
findings.explanation: People may make different decisions about information sharing and output verification.
findings.limitation: This comes from your answers. The app did not inspect business policies or establish a legal obligation.
findings.action: Agree which tools and data types are permitted, who approves exceptions and when outputs need human checking.
findings.verification: Keep the approved rules and confirm that relevant people received them.

findings.title: Check the conditions for sensitive information
findings.evidence: You reported entering sensitive information into AI tools for work.
findings.explanation: The appropriate treatment depends on the product, account tier, settings, contracts and information involved.
findings.limitation: The app did not read your inputs or vendor contracts. It has not established that a disclosure or breach occurred.
findings.action: Have the responsible owner confirm permitted information, retention, training settings and contractual protections before further sensitive use.
findings.verification: Retain the approval decision and relevant settings evidence; obtain specialist advice for restricted data.

catalog.coverage: 12 selected U.S. framework / policy / legal-source entries; 12 authored evidence work packages. Not the complete NIST framework or a complete legal crosswalk.
catalog.excluded: Other state and local laws, education / FERPA, credit / ECOA / FCRA, insurance rules, children / COPPA, biometrics, medical-device rules, frontier-model rules, national-security uses, contracts and internal policies are not comprehensively mapped. International standards used in the U.S., including ISO/IEC 42001, are not mapped.
catalog.update_mode: Bundled offline snapshot. No live legal update check; review primary sources and implementing rules before reliance. A review window is not a guarantee sources remain current.
catalog.mapping_basis: Mappings are authored readiness aids, not official NIST equivalences, legal opinions, audits or compliance determinations.
